title: Brisket-Style Beef Sandwiches
shortDescription: Brisket vibes without an overnight cook
subtitle: Smoky sliced roast, au jus dip, and pickled onions for ten
description: Chuck roast gets a BBQ-forward rub and smoke, then finishes wrapped until slice-tender. Serve on toasted rolls with a peppery au jus and quick pickled onions.

steps.title: Quick pickle the onions
steps.instruction: Heat vinegar with sugar and pepper until dissolved. Pour over sliced onion. Let sit 30 minutes.

steps.title: Rub the roast
steps.instruction: Coat roast with mustard. Mix salt, pepper, paprika, garlic, and sugar; rub all sides. Heat smoker to 275°F.

steps.title: Smoke to color
steps.instruction: Smoke 2–2.5 hours until bark is dark and internal hits ~165°F.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap tightly in foil. Finish at 275°F until probe-tender and 200–205°F, about 60–90 minutes.

steps.title: Au jus
steps.instruction: Simmer broth with Worcestershire and a pinch of pepper. Taste and salt lightly; keep hot.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 20 minutes. Slice against the grain. Toast rolls. Tonight’s board: sandwiches + au jus cups + pickled onions.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Chop into tacos or hash. Reheat slices in hot au jus so they stay juicy.

proTips: Chuck slices best after a short rest—don’t rush the knife.
Use the au jus as the reheat method.
If slices shred, it’s overcooked—serve as ‘chopped beef sandwiches’.
tonightSpread: Sliced beef on a tray, au jus in a pot, pickled onions, toasted rolls.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It scratches the brisket itch with a timeline that fits a shift. Slices clean, dips well, and holds hot without turning dry.
mealPrepNotes: Smoke early. Once wrapped, it can finish in the oven. Hold the roast wrapped in a warm box, slice right before service.
substitutions: No smoker? Roast covered at 300°F with 1 tsp smoked paprika extra; finish same temps.
